proof:
Let $\ell$ be piecewise affine on $[0,3]$ with successive integer values $0,\log 100,\log 100,0$. Its slopes are nonincreasing, so $e^{\ell(z)}\mathbf1_{[0,3]}(z)g(x)$ is jointly log-concave for any log-concave probability density $g$ with full-dimensional support. Its sampled mass is $202$. For the two outer endpoints the full chord has four unit weights, so the best minimum of its inclusive tail sums is two. For each pair with base separation two the full chord weights are $(1,10,100)$ or its reverse, giving best minimum $100$ at the high endpoint. For adjacent sites the best minimum is the larger of the two endpoint masses, in each case $100$. Taking a coarser subgrid on any chord can only remove positive terms from the two tails at a retained index. The best single-fiber mass is also $100$. These are limitations of the two certificates: for example, choose $g$ uniform on a centrally symmetric convex body with center $0$. At $(1,0)$ a through-point halfspace contains the centered continuous trace of each fiber with favorable base margin. Such fibers have combined weight at least $101$ for either sign of the base coefficient. Each contributes at least half its weight, and a pure-base normal takes whole fibers. Thus this product has normalized depth at least $1/4\ge\Gamma_d/2$, using $(1+1/d)^d\ge2$.

For the radialization claim, use the jointly log-concave density $f(z,x)=e^z\mathbf1_{[0,2]\times[-1,1]}(z,x)$ in one continuous dimension. The centered radial-integral interval at base $z$ has endpoints given by the negatives and positives of the two ray integrals $\int_0^\infty f(z,\pm r)\,dr=e^z$. The endpoint-fiber points $(0,1)$ and $(2,e^2)$ have midpoint $(1,(1+e^2)/2)$. Strict convexity of the exponential places it outside the interval at base $1$.

statement: The sampled jointly log-concave class contains a one-base-coordinate product with masses $(1,100,100,1)$ at $0,1,2,3$. For this table the best single-fiber mass and the best minimum of the two geometric tail sums in the chord bound are both $100<101=M/2$. Independently, a jointly log-concave density can have centered Ball radial-integral fibers that fail the convex-body midpoint inclusion even at integer bases.
title: Geometric chord bounds and fiberwise radialization have limits under joint log-concavity
